A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProxySPEX study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and matchable despite pagination changes. The additional checklist in v2 is also available.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution experiments on four datasets, synthetic proxy-model evaluations, CIFAR-10 interaction analyses, and MMLU attention-head pruning results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Shapley-value approximation experiments against KernelSHAP in Section 4.3 and Appendix B.5.

M1.justification: Random masking, cross-validated gradient-boosted trees, Fourier extraction and sparsification, and optional coefficient regression remain unchanged. Shapley conversion was already provided in v1 Appendix A.1; its new evaluation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: The four main datasets, CIFAR-10 and MMLU case studies, and synthetic hierarchical/non-hierarchical scenarios are retained. The Shapley experiments reuse the existing feature-attribution problems with different evaluation targets and metrics, without expanding represented data or underlying task coverage.

E2.justification: KernelSHAP becomes an explicitly evaluated comparator in v2 Figures 8 and 14, whereas v1 only discusses SHAP in the literature and baseline rationale. Existing LASSO, SPEX, proxy-model, and pruning comparators remain. LeverageSHAP and SVARM are mentioned without corresponding plotted comparison results.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix B.5 introduce a substantial additional evaluation protocol: a 10,000-mask KernelSHAP estimate as reference, Recall@10 and Shapley MSE, and inference budgets of alpha times n log2(n), with alpha in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}. This extends evaluation beyond the retained faithfulness, feature-removal, and pruning protocols; it does not revise their settings.

E4.justification: The hierarchy measurements, sparsification studies, proxy-model comparisons, non-hierarchical synthetic failure example, and both case studies are retained. The added Shapley plots provide benchmark comparisons under additional metrics rather than a separate component ablation, robustness test, or diagnostic error analysis.

E5.justification: The new Shapley plots explicitly define error bands as standard deviations across ten algorithm runs. v1 has no corresponding ten-run Shapley uncertainty reporting. This addition does not establish an increase in repetitions for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 8 and 14 add substantial Shapley-approximation results across all four main datasets and four budgets. ProxySPEX has lower MSE throughout the plotted range; its recall remains higher on three datasets, while KernelSHAP overtakes it on DROP at alpha 0.75 and 1.0. Earlier faithfulness, timing, pruning, and CIFAR-10 results are retained. These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The Fourier definitions, hierarchy metrics, conversion formulas, extraction algorithm, and integer-program derivation are unchanged, including Appendices A–C. The new empirical Shapley metrics introduce no substantive mathematical definition, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract newly emphasizes scalable Shapley approximation, and the introduction claims better approximation than KernelSHAP in the low-inference regime. The central hierarchical-interaction explanation and roughly tenfold inference-efficiency claim remain unchanged. Feature-removal and pruning contributions remain elsewhere despite reduced abstract emphasis.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds a qualification explaining KernelSHAP's eventual advantage through ProxySPEX's faithfulness objective and lack of Shapley-kernel weighting. Section 3.3 also comments on the typically marginal benefit of optional regression. Existing limitations concerning non-hierarchical interactions, proxy fidelity, and human interpretability remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit implementation pointer to the shapiq repository in the abstract and code/data availability statements in the checklist. Existing hyperparameter grids, masking instructions, prompts, hardware, and runtime details are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not independent verification of repository contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Mohammadi et al., LeverageSHAP, and SVARM, distinguishes function-approximation and axiomatic attribution formulations, and adds a paragraph contrasting SPEX's structured sampling with ProxySPEX's random-sample proxy fitting. Numerous other reference edits update publication metadata rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: The scientific narrative remains largely intact. Local abstract, introduction, related-work, and regression-step edits accompany new Sections 4.3 and B.5, updated bibliography entries, and an appended NeurIPS checklist. The main organization is preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds four-panel Shapley recall and MSE figures with uncertainty bands, adds an explicit method-color legend to the retained timing figure, and relocates several figures as text reflows. Existing tables, diagrams, and result displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The direct KernelSHAP comparisons, defined ten-run uncertainty, clearer relationship to SPEX, and implementation pointer improve empirical support and usability while preserving the original evidence. The gains are limited: Shapley reference values are themselves approximations, and the broad eventual-crossover language is only partly demonstrated by the plotted budgets, with a visible recall crossover on DROP.
